record.original_question: Can the subspace-completion approach used in Wigner distribution deconvolution be generalized so that it can recover a signal when an arbitrary number of Fourier coefficients are missing, while still keeping the computational cost reasonable?

evidence.quote: Question 8.2. Can a version of SC be designed to handle an arbitrary number of missing coefficients with a reasonable operational cost?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $f \in \mathbb{C}^N$ be an unknown signal whose discrete Fourier transform $\hat f \in \mathbb{C}^N$ we wish to recover from intensity-only ptychographic measurements. In Wigner distribution deconvolution (WDD), one collects, for a known window/probe $w \in \mathbb{C}^N$ and a set of translates $\{T_\ell w\}_{\ell}$, the squared moduli $|\langle f, M_k T_\ell w\rangle|^2$, where $M_k$ and $T_\ell$ denote modulation and translation operators. These measurements give access, via a 2D Fourier transform, to entries of the Wigner-type matrix
$$X_{j,k} \;=\; \hat f(j)\,\overline{\hat f(j+k)}\,\cdot\, c_{j,k}(w),$$
where $c_{j,k}(w)$ are known coefficients depending on the window. After deconvolving by the known window factors, one obtains (a subset of) the rank-one matrix $\hat f \hat f^*$, from which $\hat f$ is recovered up to a global phase.

In practice some Fourier coefficients of the window vanish (or are too small to invert stably), so certain off-diagonals of $\hat f \hat f^*$ are missing. The subspace completion (SC) method exploits the rank-one structure of $\hat f \hat f^*$ to recover a small number of missing diagonals by solving a low-dimensional eigenvector problem on accessible blocks. Standard SC is designed for the case where only a few off-diagonals are inaccessible, and its operational cost grows rapidly with the number of missing off-diagonals.

Problem. Design and analyze a generalization of the subspace completion technique that provably recovers $\hat f$ (up to a global phase) from the available entries of $\hat f \hat f^*$ when an arbitrary number of off-diagonals (equivalently, an arbitrary subset of Fourier coefficients of the window) are missing, while keeping the total computational cost reasonable (e.g.\ polynomial in $N$, and ideally near-linear or matching the cost of a small number of FFTs). Provide both an algorithm and conditions on the missing-pattern under which exact or stable recovery is guaranteed.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an explicit open problem in a 2025 survey on open problems in phase retrieval arising from the PRiMA workshop. No subsequent work resolving the generalized subspace-completion question with reasonable operational cost was located.

status_evidence.snippet: Survey of selected open problems in phase retrieval, outcome of the PRiMA workshop (Lorentz Center, 2024).
status_evidence.claim: The problem is listed among open problems in the 2025 phase retrieval survey, with no resolution noted.
